lessons.title: Rounding to the nearest 100
objectives: Round numbers to the nearest 100
Decide using the tens digit

keywords.def: the closest multiple of one hundred
exactly in the middle between two numbers

teach.heading: Between hundreds
teach.note: Use the number line with 450 marked. Compare with rounding to 10.

teach.heading: The tens digit decides
bullets: 0 to 4: stay the same, ones go to zero.
teach.note: Show 463 -> tens digit 6 -> up to 500. And 438 -> tens digit 3 -> down to 400.

teach.heading: Bigger numbers
teach.note: Work through the carrying: 6,951 has tens digit 5 so round up to 7,000. Check by number line.

teach.heading: Error trap
bullets: Do not look at the ones digit.
Check the digit to the right.
teach.note: A common error is rounding 349 to 350 and then to 400. Rounding is done in one step, using only the digit to the right.

independent: A number rounds to 600. What is the smallest it could be? The largest?
Is 2,349 closer to 2,300 or 2,400? Explain.

lessons.send: SEND: scaffold with a number line and highlight the deciding digit. Stretch: rounding to the nearest 1000 and 10,000.

lessons.title: Bridge: Roman numerals to 100
lessons.bigQuestion: How did the Romans write numbers without a zero?
objectives: To understand how Roman numerals work and why place value is better
successCriteria: All: read numerals to 20
Most: write numerals to 100
Some: explain the subtraction rule (IV, IX, XL, XC)
lessons.crossCurricular: History: Roman Britain; clock faces and book chapters
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: Muslim scholars spread the Hindu-Arabic numerals with zero, which made calculation easier

keywords.def: letters the Romans used for numbers
our system: a digit's value depends on its place

hook.text: Some clocks show IV for 4 and IX for 9. Why might IV be 4?
hook.a: I before V means 1 less than 5. A smaller numeral before a bigger one is subtracted.

islamicLink.text: Muslim mathematicians such as al-Khwarizmi (الخوارزمي) in Baghdad wrote about calculating with the Hindu-Arabic digits and zero, which spread to Europe and replaced Roman numerals.

pictures.alt: A clock face with Roman numerals
A page from al-Khwarizmi's book on calculation

teach.heading: Subtract when smaller first
teach.note: Only I before V or X; X before L or C.

independent.q: Core: XVII, XXXV, LIV
Extend: write 49, 64 and 91.
Stretch: why is there no symbol for 0? How does our zero help?
independent.a: Roman numerals have no place value; our 0 holds empty places, like in 105

exit.q: Write 38 in Roman numerals.
exit.a: XXXVIII

exit.q: Big question: what does XC mean and why?
exit.a: 90: X before C means 100 - 10

lessons.title: Negative numbers in context
objectives: Understand negative numbers using temperature
Order numbers including negatives

keywords.def: how hot or cold something is, in degrees Celsius
the number between positive and negative

teach.heading: Below zero
teach.note: Use a thermometer picture. Introduce the minus sign. Ask where negative numbers are used: temperatures, bank overdraft, floors below ground.

teach.heading: Number line
teach.note: Draw a line from -10 to 10. Point out that -2 is greater than -5 because it is further right.

teach.heading: Ordering
teach.note: Common error: thinking -7 is bigger than -2 because 7 is bigger than 2. Use temperature: -7 is colder.

teach.heading: Counting through zero
teach.note: Practise in steps of 1 and 2. Ask: how many steps from -3 to 2? (5)

independent: The temperature is 3 degrees. It falls by 5 degrees. What is the temperature now?
A lift goes from floor 2 down to floor -3. How many floors does it move?
exit: The temperature is -2 and rises by 5. What is it now?
lessons.homework: Look at a weather forecast for another country this week. Write down the temperatures and order them.
lessons.send: SEND: use a vertical thermometer model. Stretch: find differences between temperatures such as 8 and -5.

teach.heading: Odd one out

teach.heading: True or false
